items.followUp: Define weight and state its SI unit.

rubric.description: Defines mass as the amount or quantity of matter in a body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition of mass.

rubric.description: States kilogram (kg) as the SI unit of mass.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct SI unit.

modelAnswer: Mass is the amount of matter in a body.

items.followUp: A motor does 60 J of work in 5 s. Find its power.

rubric.why: Power is the rate of doing work.
rubric.description: Uses the relation power = work ÷ time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

rubric.why: The calculation gives the machine's power.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: Work, W = 4 J; time, t = 2 s.
Formula: P = W/t.
Substitution: P = 4 J/2 s = 2 J s⁻¹.
Answer: P = 2 W.

items.followUp: Define work and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: This is the defining meaning of power.
rubric.description: Defines power as the rate of doing work or work done per unit time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

rubric.why: The SI unit must be identified.
rubric.description: States watt (W) as the SI unit of power.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct SI unit.

modelAnswer: Power is the rate of doing work.
Its SI unit is the watt (W).

rubric.why: The standard conversion factor is needed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct conversion factor or equivalent setup.
Award 1 mark for the correct converted answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: P = 1120 W; 1 hp = 746 W.
Formula: Power in hp = power in W ÷ 746.
Substitution: P = 1120 W ÷ 746 W/hp ≈ 1.50 hp.
Answer: P ≈ 1.50 hp.

items.followUp: Define density and write its mathematical formula.

rubric.why: This is the definition of pressure.
rubric.description: Defines pressure as force acting per unit area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

rubric.why: The required mathematical relation is pressure equals force divided by area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

modelAnswer: Pressure is the force acting per unit area of a surface.
Mathematical formula: P = F/A.

items.followUp: State Hooke's law and explain what happens when the elastic limit is exceeded.

rubric.why: Hooke's law applies only while the elastic limit is not exceeded.
rubric.description: States that extension is directly proportional to the applied force, provided the elastic limit is not exceeded.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the proportional relationship and its condition.

rubric.why: The elastic limit concerns recovery of the body's original shape after the force is removed.
rubric.description: Explains that up to the elastic limit, the body returns to its original shape when the deforming force is removed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct explanation of the elastic limit.

modelAnswer: Hooke's law states that extension is directly proportional to the applied force, provided the elastic limit is not exceeded.
The elastic limit is the limit up to which a body regains its original shape when the deforming force is removed.

items.followUp: Define specific heat capacity and temperature.

rubric.why: Heat is energy transferred because of a temperature difference.
rubric.description: Defines heat as energy transferred from a hotter body to a colder body due to a temperature difference.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a definition that identifies heat as transferred energy.

rubric.why: Temperature describes how hot or cold a body is.
rubric.description: Defines temperature as the degree of hotness or coldness of a body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition of temperature.

modelAnswer: Heat is energy transferred from a hotter body to a colder body because of a temperature difference.
Temperature is the degree of hotness or coldness of a body.

items.followUp: Suggest two ways to reduce energy use in a school building.

rubric.why: Switching off unused electrical devices prevents unnecessary energy use.
rubric.description: Suggests switching off lights or appliances when they are not needed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this or another sensible measure to avoid unnecessary electricity use.

rubric.why: Efficient devices, insulation, or daylight reduce energy demand in the house.
rubric.description: Suggests an energy-saving measure such as using efficient bulbs/appliances, insulation, or natural light.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one suitable additional measure.

modelAnswer: Switch off lights and electrical appliances when they are not in use.
Use energy-efficient bulbs and appliances, and make use of daylight where possible.
